records.name: Congregation Leyv Ha-Ir (Heart of the City)
records.summary: A small Reconstructionist congregation that meets mostly at the Ethical Society building near Rittenhouse Square. Members take part in worship, holiday events, adult classes, social justice work, and the choir.
records.what_you_do: Join worship services and holiday events, sign up for adult education or social justice projects, or sing in the choir. The congregation offers lower-cost dues options.

schedule.text: The site does not print service times. Check the events calendar for dates.

cost.text: Membership and dues options exist. Amounts are not printed on the site.

first_step.how: Browse the events calendar and register for an event, or contact the congregation about joining
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly and there is a clear way to join, but the site does not say whether guests may attend services.

records.notes: The congregation site lists only a P.O. Box, so the Rittenhouse address comes from the Reconstructing Judaism page. The site shows no dated items, so status is probably_active.

records.name: Kol Tzedek
records.summary: A Reconstructionist synagogue in West Philadelphia. Members pray on Shabbat, study in the Torah school and adult classes, and can join a virtual community.
records.what_you_do: Come to Shabbat and prayer services, enroll children in the Torah school, take an adult learning class, or become a member. A newsletter sign-up is on the site.

schedule.text: Shabbat services at 5300 Whitby Ave. Times are on the Shabbat and prayer page, which was not read for this record.

cost.text: A membership page and a sustaining share are listed. Dues amounts are not printed.

first_step.how: Use the Shabbat and prayer page or the membership page, or send a general question through the site
first_step.basis: Membership and prayer pages are public, but the site does not say whether guests are welcome.

records.notes: The site lists an office at 5310 Whitby Ave and Shabbat services at 5300 Whitby Ave. An older listing gives 707 S. 50th St, which was not used. The general email is hidden on the site and was not recorded. The events section has no dated items.

records.name: Congregation B'nai Israel Ohev Zedek
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia synagogue with daily prayer services, weekly Torah classes, and youth groups on Shabbat. The site has a page for visitors who want to spend a Shabbos there.
records.what_you_do: Pray at Shabbat or weekday services, attend the Torah classes, bring children to the youth groups, or sponsor a kiddush or a Shalosh Seudos meal. The membership form is online.

schedule.text: Shabbat services on Saturday morning with Shacharis at 9:00 am, Friday evening candle lighting with Mincha and Maariv, and weekday Shacharis each morning. The times printed on the site were for the Ha'azinu weekend, so confirm before you go.

cost.text: Membership and donation options are listed. Amounts are not printed.

first_step.how: Visit for a Shabbos, using the site's visiting page, or contact the shul by email
first_step.basis: The site has a page for visiting on Shabbos and a contact route, so a newcomer knows how to start.

records.notes: A program listed with the date 13 Oct 26 and a September 2026 newsletter are the dated evidence. The Ha'azinu weekend times on the site are for September 18 and 19, 2026, and are past.

records.name: Congregation Ahavas Torah
records.summary: A shul in Northeast Philadelphia with about 100 member families. It holds daily prayer services and regular Torah classes (shiurim) led by its rav.
records.what_you_do: Join a daily minyan or a shiur, take part in the Shabbos hospitality program for visitors, or apply for membership through the membership page.

schedule.text: The site says there are daily minyanim and links to an external davening schedule and a separate shiur schedule. Times are not printed on the pages read.

cost.text: Membership is listed. Dues are not printed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Use the Shabbos hospitality page or the Contact Us page
first_step.basis: Hospitality and contact pages are listed, but the site does not describe how visitors are welcomed.

records.notes: The address comes from the Map and Directions page. The site shows no dated items, and no email or phone is printed on the pages read.

records.name: Jewish Community of Rhawnhurst (JCOR)
records.summary: An Orthodox community network in Rhawnhurst, Northeast Philadelphia. It links six congregations, a kollel, chesed groups, schools, and mikvahs, and it shares the weekly eruv status.
records.what_you_do: Join the JCOR email group for announcements, shiurim, events, and job and housing listings. Check the weekly eruv status, or browse the shul directory to choose a congregation.

schedule.text: No meeting times are printed. Shiurim and events are announced through the email group.

cost.text: No fees are listed for the email group.

first_step.how: Join the JCOR email group from the website, or watch the introductory video
first_step.basis: The site invites people to visit or move to the community and has a sign-up route for announcements.

records.notes: The page has no dated items. The copyright footer is not evidence. Phone numbers on the page belong to other groups and were not recorded. The Northeast Community Kollel it names is in leads_only.

records.name: Lubavitch Center for Russian Jewry (Bustleton)
records.summary: A Chabad center on Byberry Road in Bustleton with its own shul, a Hebrew school, a Sunday program, a teen club, and women's gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Attend services at the shul, enroll children in the Hebrew school or Sunday program, join the teen club or a women's circle, or ask the rabbi a question online.

schedule.text: Shabbat services, Hebrew school, and a Sunday program. The site does not print regular days or times.

cost.text: The Hebrew school has tuition. Amounts are on its registration page, which was not read.

first_step.how: Ask the rabbi through the site's question form, or call 215-514-0729
first_step.basis: Clear ways to ask questions and join the mailing list are listed, but the site does not say how visitors are welcomed at services.

records.notes: The weekly Torah portion item is linked with the date 10/8/2026. Photo galleries run from 2016 to 2023 and were not used as evidence. The men's mikvah at the Philadelphia Lubavitcher Center is a separate listing and was not recorded.

records.name: CBS Community Center (Congregation Beth Solomon)
records.summary: A Jewish community center on Tomlinson Road in Northeast Philadelphia with davening services, a kollel, a mikvah, and programs for men, women, and youth.
records.what_you_do: Join davening services, men's learning or women's programming, youth programs, or the Pesach food drive. Sign up for weekly updates on the site.

schedule.text: Davening times and High Holiday schedules are on separate pages that the homepage does not show.

cost.text: No fees are printed on the homepage. Donations are invited.

first_step.how: Email or call the office to ask how to join a program
first_step.basis: Programs are listed, but the site does not say whether visitors can join or how a newcomer starts.

records.notes: The only date on the site is a 2024 copyright footer, which is not evidence. The site does not say whether programs are open to non-members, so open_to needs checking. The daycare it lists is not recorded as a group.

records.name: Mitzvah Food Program
records.summary: A food pantry program run by the Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia. It runs pantries across the region, including one in Bustleton in Northeast Philadelphia, and it delivers food to people who need it.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the online form, donate food or gift cards, or ask for help through the new client form. The fall High Holiday Drive collects grocery store gift cards.

schedule.text: Bustleton pantry: Wednesdays and Thursdays 10 am to 3:30 pm, Fridays 10 am to 1 pm, and Tuesday afternoons by appointment only. Call before you come.

cost.text: The site lists no fee for food and asks for donations.

first_step.how: Fill out the online new client form, or call 215.832.0831 for walk-in and emergency help at Bustleton
first_step.basis: Walk-in hours are listed and new clients can apply online. The pantry serves anyone in need.

records.notes: faith is left null on purpose, not jewish as the brief asked, because the program says pantries serve everyone in need regardless of religion. The orchestrator should decide. The Bustleton pantry has no street address on the page. The Bala Cynwyd, Bensalem and Elkins Park pantries are outside the city and are not recorded as locations. Dated items are social posts with no year, so status is probably_active.

records.name: Mishkan Shalom
records.summary: A Reconstructionist congregation in Roxborough with Shabbat services, a Hebrew school, a choir, a men's group, spiritual direction, and a Rosh Chodesh gathering.
records.what_you_do: Come to Shabbat services, join the choir or the Men of Mishkan group, or enroll children in the Hebrew school or the family b'nai mitzvah classes. Membership levels and an application are on the site.

schedule.text: The site lists a Shabbat service on Saturday, October 10, 10 am to noon, and a Rosh Chodesh gathering on Sunday, October 11, 4 to 5 pm. Hebrew school, choir, and men's group also have listed times.

cost.text: Membership levels are listed. Amounts are not printed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Go to the join page, or call the office at 215-508-0226 (office hours Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm)
first_step.basis: Join and event pages are public, but the site does not explain how a first visit works or whether guests may attend.

records.notes: The homepage is dated Thursday, October 8, 2026. Personal email addresses printed on the site were left out. The 1299 Church Road address in the page footer belongs to Reconstructing Judaism, not the congregation.

records.name: Vilna Congregation
records.summary: A congregation on Pine Street in Philadelphia led by Rabbi Menachem Schmidt. The website does not list service times or classes, so visitors contact the rabbi directly.
records.what_you_do: Contact Rabbi Schmidt to ask about services and learning, or support the congregation with an online donation.

schedule.text: The website does not list service times. Ask the rabbi.

cost.text: The site lists no dues. It has an online donation form.

first_step.how: Email or call the rabbi (contact details are on the website)
first_step.basis: The website asks people to contact the rabbi, but it does not describe services, classes, or how a newcomer joins.

records.notes: No dated items and no service or class listings on the site. The rabbi's personal email printed on the site was left out. Mikvah Mei Shalva (philamikvah.org), linked from the site, is a separate listing.

records.name: Congregation Mikveh Israel
records.summary: A historic congregation at 44 North Fourth Street. It offers weekday morning and afternoon prayer services with a free breakfast or lunch, Shabbat services, public tours, and a museum exhibit.
records.what_you_do: Join the weekday morning Shaharit or the afternoon Minha minyan, take the historic synagogue tour, see the Faith and Freedom exhibition, or join the WhatsApp group for a minyan.

schedule.text: Weekday Shaharit at 7:15 am on Mondays and Thursdays and on Rosh Chodesh. Minha at 2 pm, Monday to Thursday. This week's Shabbat times: Friday 6:15 pm and Saturday 9 am (Shabbat Bereishit).

cost.text: The site lists free breakfast or lunch and free parking with the weekday minyanim.

first_step.how: Join the WhatsApp group for the weekday minyan, sign up for the newsletter, or book a public tour
first_step.basis: Public tours and group chats are listed. The site does not say that newcomers are welcomed directly.

records.notes: A July 11, 2026 item reports storm damage to the congregation's cemetery at 8th and Spruce Streets and asks for donations. It is not recorded as a volunteer opportunity. The upcoming events area shows placeholder text. Wikipedia lists the Spanish and Portuguese (Sephardic) rite.

records.name: Germantown Jewish Centre
records.summary: A congregation at 400 West Ellet Street that serves the Jewish community in Northwest Philadelphia. It runs Friday night services, weekly Torah study, adult learning, a religious school, a choir, and a Hazak group for people 55 and older.
records.what_you_do: Attend Friday night services, join Weekly Torah Study with the rabbi, take an adult class at Koleinu Beit Midrash, or join the men's club, Women of GJC, the choir, or Hazak. Families can enroll children in the religious school or early childhood program.

schedule.text: Friday night services, weekday services, weekly Torah study, adult learning, a religious school, and programs for children and teens. Most pages read do not print days or times.

cost.text: Membership information is on the site. Dues are not stated.

first_step.how: Use the Join the Community page, or register for the weekly Torah study
first_step.basis: Join and registration pages are public. The site does not say whether non-members can attend programs.

records.notes: The dated item is a rabbi's blog post dated Monday, February 16, 2026. The denomination is from a Wikipedia listing, not the congregation's site. The 90th anniversary program is dated November 2025.

records.name: Congregation Rodeph Shalom
records.summary: A Center City congregation on North Broad Street with Friday evening and Saturday morning services, Saturday Torah study, and a weekly Wednesday morning gathering called Breaking Bread on Broad.
records.what_you_do: Come to Friday evening or Saturday morning services, join Saturday Torah study or the Wednesday morning gathering, or watch services by livestream. The site has a New to Judaism page for people new to the faith.

schedule.text: Friday pre-oneg at 5:30 pm, Friday Shabbat evening service at 6:00 pm, Saturday Torah study at 9:15 am, Saturday morning service at 10:45 am, and Breaking Bread on Broad on Wednesday mornings. Holiday services are on the full calendar.

cost.text: Membership and dues are not stated on the page. Online donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Use the New to Judaism page or the Join Our Community page linked on the site, or call the office at 215.627.6747
first_step.basis: The site has a page for people new to Judaism and a join page, plus office hours, so a newcomer knows how to start. The guest policy is not stated.

records.notes: The site's weather closure notice has no printed date. The denomination is not stated on the pages read, so it is not recorded. The entry is at 1339 Green St.

records.name: B'nai Abraham Chabad
records.summary: A Chabad congregation at 527 Lombard Street that invites Jews of all backgrounds to study, pray, and make friends. It offers adult Torah study, a preschool, and a Hebrew school.
records.what_you_do: Join a season of Torah studies, a weekly class, a High Holiday or minyan service, a Kiddush, or a Mitzvah opportunity. Membership details are on a separate page.

schedule.text: Service, class, and event times are not printed on the homepage. It links to pages for High Holidays, minyans, weekly and upcoming classes, and events.

cost.text: Membership is listed on a separate page. Amounts were not read.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-238-2100, or use the site's contact route
first_step.basis: The site invites people of all backgrounds to join and lists a phone number. It does not describe a first visit.

records.notes: The Torah study seasons are titled with Hebrew year 5786 (about 2025 to 2026), which is the newest dated evidence. No Gregorian date is printed. The email on the site is obscured and was not recorded. The Chabad of Center City named by Federation and Jewish Exponent sources may be this same group, which is unconfirmed.

records.name: Chabad House at the University of Pennsylvania (Chabad at Penn)
records.summary: The Chabad house at the University of Pennsylvania on Spruce Street. It has pages for students, graduate students, and alumni, and it posts candle lighting times and holiday RSVPs.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for event updates through the Chabad Bot, join the mailing list or the Students Weekly Newsletter, or RSVP for holiday and family events. Contact the house through its contact page.

schedule.text: No recurring service or class times are printed on the page. It shows weekly candle lighting and Shabbat end times.

cost.text: No fees are printed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Sign up for the Chabad Bot or the mailing list, then RSVP for an event
first_step.basis: The site has sign-up and RSVP routes for events. The page does not say explicitly that newcomers are welcome.

records.notes: The site shows a Friday, October 9 candle lighting time and a Pesach 2026 page link, but no printed year beside the October dates, so status is probably_active. The site prints its address as 4032 to 4034 Spruce Street. The Penn club listing gives 4032 Spruce Street, which is used here. The email came from the Penn club listing, not the house site. Chabad Serving Drexel is a separate house, listed in leads_only.

records.name: Temple Beth Zion-Beth Israel (BZBI)
records.summary: A congregation at 300 South 18th Street in Center City. It holds Shabbat morning services in person and on Zoom, weekday morning minyanim, early childhood and family education, and adult learning.
records.what_you_do: Join Shabbat morning services or a weekday minyan, plan a first visit with the Visiting Us page, take part in adult learning, or join a Shabbat dinner for young professionals. Membership and dues pages are linked.

schedule.text: Shabbat morning service at 9:30 am in the Goldberg Sanctuary and on Zoom. Weekday minyanim on Monday and Thursday, Tuesday and Wednesday, and Friday morning, plus a Sunday morning minyan and schmooze. Times are on the worship page.

cost.text: Membership and dues pages are linked. Amounts are not printed on the homepage.

first_step.how: Use the Visiting Us page, or call 215.735.5148 or email templeoffice@bzbi.org
first_step.basis: The site has a Visiting Us page and listed contacts. It does not describe a first visit or guest policy.

records.notes: The event dates on the homepage appear only in link addresses, for example Shabbat services on 2026-10-10 and a Sisterhood meeting on 2026-11-02. Many other events are listed with no dates. The only visible text is the group's own pages.

records.name: Society Hill Synagogue
records.summary: A congregation at 418 Spruce Street in Society Hill with Friday evening and Saturday morning services, a weekly Monday evening minyan on Zoom, a playschool for children ages 18 months to 5, and a Hebrew school.
records.what_you_do: Join Shabbat services and the meals after them, take an adult education class, enroll a child in the playschool or Hebrew school, or join the Monday evening minyan on Zoom. Membership renewals are done through an online form.

schedule.text: Friday evening and Saturday morning Shabbat services in the sanctuary, a weekly Monday evening minyan on Zoom, and Shabbat and holiday meals after services. The site does not print times.

cost.text: Dues and school tuition are paid through a link on the site. Amounts are not listed.

first_step.how: Call 215-922-6590 or join through the membership form on the site
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, and it has a membership form. It does not describe a first visit or guest policy.

records.notes: The events list shows a loading message on the page, so no dated items were found. No email is printed on the page.

records.name: Mekor Habracha (Center City Synagogue)
records.summary: A congregation at 1500 Walnut Street that welcomes visitors. It runs daily minyanim and classes on its davening schedule, a monthly Tot Shabbat for young children, and a WhatsApp group.
records.what_you_do: Join the WhatsApp group or the newsletter, come to the monthly Tot Shabbat for young children, attend a minyan or class on the davening schedule, or sponsor a Kiddush.

schedule.text: Daily minyanim and classes are on the davening schedule page, which was not read. The homepage lists a Tot Shabbat once a month, with no time printed.

cost.text: Membership is listed. Dues and fees are not stated on the page.

first_step.how: Join the WhatsApp group or sign up for the newsletter, both linked from the homepage
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are welcomed and links newsletter and WhatsApp sign-ups.

records.notes: The upcoming events and Hebrew date displays were still loading, so no dated items were read. The davening schedule page was not read.

records.name: P'nai Or Philadelphia
records.summary: A congregation in West Mount Airy that meets in the Community Wing of Summit Presbyterian Church. Its Saturday services include morning prayer and a Torah service, followed by a potluck lunch and a Zoom option.
records.what_you_do: Come to Saturday morning services in person or on Zoom, join the Torah service and breakout discussion, bring a dish to the potluck, or join the Zoom Torah study from home led by the rabbi.

schedule.text: Saturday morning Shacharit from 10:30 am to noon, in person and on Zoom. Torah service from noon to 1 pm, potluck at 1 pm, and a Zoom shmooze at 2:30 pm. The Zoom Torah study from home runs 9:15 to 10:15 am on a day the site does not state.

cost.text: Dues are not listed. A recommended donation applies to the High Holy Days.

first_step.how: Come on a Saturday, in person or on Zoom. For Zoom study, read the Torah Study info sheet linked on the site.
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome, members or not, and that no prior knowledge is needed. It also explains how to join the Zoom study.

records.notes: High Holy Days 5787/2026 is listed with Eventbrite registration, but no month is printed. The site's news items are undated, and their links suggest 2023. The email on the site looks like a personal account, so it was left out.

records.name: The Little Shul (Congregation Shivtei Yeshuron Ezras Israel)
records.summary: A small South Philadelphia shul at 2015 South 4th Street. It holds Shabbos services once a month, on the first Saturday, and on the second Saturday when a holiday falls on the first.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly Shabbos service (no tickets or reservations are needed), join the membership list, or sign up for the newsletter. The site also takes donations toward its building and security funds.

schedule.text: Shabbos services on the first Saturday of each month at 10 am. On holiday weekends they move to the second Saturday. The site lists upcoming services on Saturday, October 3, Saturday, November 7, and Saturday, December 5, printed without a year.

cost.text: No tickets are needed for services. Membership and donation options exist. Amounts are not printed.

first_step.how: Come to a monthly service. No tickets or reservations are needed.
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome and that no reservations are needed for services.

records.notes: The 2026 schedule is an image that could not be read. The site has a contact page only, with no email or phone printed. Upcoming dates are printed without a year.
